tool_args.old_string: The two temporal cohorts differ in base/instruct composition (2023: 79.7\% base, $N_{\mathrm{base}}{=}861$, $N_{\mathrm{inst}}{=}219$; 2024: 67.9\% base, $N_{\mathrm{base}}{=}548$, $N_{\mathrm{inst}}{=}259$). Downsampling 2023 to match the 2024 ratio yields balanced C\% $= 30.25\% \pm 1.32\%$ ($\Delta = 1.08$\,pp; \Cref{app:composition_control}), ruling out composition shift. Within-architecture analysis confirms DIF is not a cross-architecture artifact: Llama-lineage models ($N{=}171/315$) yield C\% $= 59.2\%$; Qwen, Yi, and Phi also exceed the random baseline (\Cref{app:within_arch}). Within-family matching validates the same pattern: Llama-2 vs.\ Llama-3 raw C\% $= 61.3\%$ drops to $28.3\%$ after nearest-neighbor matching, consistent with temporal matched C\% ($28.9\%$).
tool_args.new_string: The two temporal cohorts differ in base/instruct composition (2023: 79.7\% vs.\ 2024: 67.9\% base). Downsampling to match ratios yields C\% $= 30.25\% \pm 1.32\%$ ($\Delta = 1.08$\,pp; \Cref{app:composition_control}), ruling out composition shift. Within-architecture DIF confirms the signal persists within individual lineages (Llama C\% $= 59.2\%$; \Cref{app:within_arch}), consistent with ability-matched temporal C\% ($28.9\%$).

tool_args.old_string: Item-level properties do not predict DIF susceptibility (AUROC $= 0.60$; \Cref{app:predictive}), precluding pre-screening. We recommend MH-DIF audits whenever ${\geq}$500 models accumulate ($K{=}3$ suffices for smaller corpora; \Cref{tab:k3_power}), with action levels calibrated to $\rho$-degradation (\Cref{app:fig_rho_degradation}). Because DIF detects differential functioning without attributing cause~\citep{camilli1994methods}, flagged items warrant mechanism-conditional responses: under contamination, remove or downweight; under capability evolution, retain but annotate; under composition shift, refine cohort definitions. DIF-corrected scoring motivates linear equating adjustments~\citep{kolen2014equating,habba2026growingpains}.
tool_args.new_string: Item-level properties do not predict DIF susceptibility (AUROC $= 0.60$; \Cref{app:predictive}), precluding pre-screening. We recommend MH-DIF audits whenever ${\geq}$500 models accumulate ($K{=}3$ for smaller corpora; \Cref{tab:k3_power}), with action thresholds calibrated to $\rho$-degradation (\Cref{app:fig_rho_degradation}). Flagged items warrant mechanism-conditional responses: remove contaminated items, annotate capability-shifted ones, or refine cohort definitions. DIF-corrected scoring motivates equating adjustments~\citep{kolen2014equating,habba2026growingpains}.

tool_args.old_string: Across six METABENCH benchmarks, 17.9--31.3\% of items exhibit temporal DIF across 2023--2024 model cohorts (${\approx}$27--29\% for MMLU; conservative bound: 13.5\%), while aggregate rankings remain preserved ($\rho \approx 0.997$). Global exposure and differential functioning are empirically independent (Jaccard $= 0.206$)---complementary dimensions confirmed by the base-vs-instruct reversal ($\chi^2 = 562.7$). DIF-corrected scoring shifts accuracy by ${+}2.12$\,pp on average, with rank displacements exceeding ${\pm}500$. We recommend mechanism-conditional audit---flag items, diagnose via exclusion arguments, then remove contaminated items, annotate capability-shifted ones, or refine cohort definitions---complementing contamination screening as standard practice~\citep{habba2026growingpains,kolen2014equating}.
tool_args.new_string: Across six METABENCH benchmarks, 17.9--31.3\% of items exhibit temporal DIF across 2023--2024 model cohorts (${\approx}$27--29\% for MMLU; conservative bound: 13.5\%), while aggregate rankings remain preserved ($\rho \approx 0.997$). Global exposure and differential functioning are complementary diagnostic dimensions (Jaccard $= 0.206$), confirmed by opposite base-vs-instruct DIF patterns ($\chi^2 = 562.7$). DIF-corrected scoring shifts accuracy by ${+}2.12$\,pp on average (rank displacements ${\pm}500{+}$). We recommend mechanism-conditional audit---complementing contamination screening as standard practice~\citep{habba2026growingpains,kolen2014equating}.

Reviewer 逐项评估了 3 个 LLM-specific 贡献：
- Cross-subject matching + ΔFPR=0: **Genuine innovation** ✓
- Family-level DEFF correction: **Domain adaptation**（DEFF/ICC 是标准 survey methodology）
- Semi-synthetic validation: **Between adaptation and innovation**

**修改要求**：
- 全文将 "three LLM-specific innovations" 改为 "three LLM-specific methodological adaptations"
- 在列举时突出 cross-subject matching 的 novelty: *"including a novel cross-subject matching strategy with constructive ΔFPR guarantee"*
- DEFF 和 semi-synthetic 用 "develop" / "adapt" 而非 "innovate"
- 跟随 R14-R1 的措辞 "methodological adaptation with domain-specific innovations"（复数 adaptations + 单数 innovation for cross-subject matching）

**2. [Important] 术语升级 — "temporal score incomparability"**

Reviewer 支持从 "measurement instability" 转为 "score incomparability"，理由：
- 机制中立（无论 contamination 还是 capability evolution，分数跨 cohort 不可直接比较）
- 与 Camilli & Shepard impact vs bias 框架对齐
- 与 score inflation 数据支撑

**但需要精确区分**：
- "Ranking comparability" = preserved (ρ ≈ 0.997)
- "Score comparability" = compromised (个体模型位移 ±561)

建议在 Introduction 或 §5.1 加一句：
*"Aggregate rankings are robust (ρ ≈ 0.997), but absolute scores are not directly comparable: the same score carries different meaning across model generations, with individual models displaced by up to 849 rank positions."*

术语方案：
- 标题和 core claim 用 "temporal score incomparability"
- "Temporal DIF" 作为技术术语
- "Measurement instability" 仅在首次出现时作为定义后的描述性简称

1	\section*{Limitations}
2	
3	\looseness=-1
4	Three primary limitations apply. (1)~The semi-synthetic framework uses uniform binary response flipping, a worst-case injection model; reported $\Delta\mathrm{TPR}$ values are upper-bound estimates, and detection power under realistic contamination patterns (partial memorization, format-specific advantages) is untested. The framework detects measurement changes but does not attribute causal mechanisms; follow-up expert review is needed to determine whether flagged items should be retired or retained. (2)~The MH $\chi^2$ test assumes independent examinees; LLM model families violate this assumption. Three convergent corrections (${\approx}$27--29\%) and family-level cluster bootstrap (95\% CI: $[26.7\%, 53.2\%]$) bound the impact, but the extreme relatedness of some families (e.g., hundreds of Llama-2 fine-tunes) exceeds the clustering levels studied in educational settings~\citep{french2010hierarchical}. (3)~Cross-subject matching assumes contamination affects a minority of domains; $\Delta\mathrm{FPR}$ rises to 0.069 when contamination spans ${\geq}20$ subjects. Temporal cohorts defined by calendar year provide coarse granularity, and generalizability to open-ended or partial-credit benchmarks is untested. Multidimensional DIF~\citep{ackerman1992didmf} may arise when MMLU's 57 subjects span distinct latent dimensions; cross-subject matching mitigates between-domain multidimensionality but not within-domain violations. IRT parameters are used only for auxiliary power analysis; all core DIF results are nonparametric.
5

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	When we say ``Model B outperforms Model A on MMLU,'' we implicitly assume that the benchmark measures the same construct in the same way for both models. This assumption of temporal comparability underpins every cross-generation comparison published on leaderboards and in model reports, yet it is rarely tested. We use \emph{measurement invariance} to denote the property that test items function identically across groups~\citep{meredith1993invariance}, \emph{differential item functioning} (DIF) as the item-level statistical test for violations, and \emph{temporal measurement instability} as the empirical phenomenon when DIF is detected across time-defined cohorts---a descriptive term denoting systematic changes in measurement properties, without implying degradation or attributing cause. Applying Mantel-Haenszel DIF analysis~\citep{holland1988mh} with ETS severity classification to the METABENCH response matrix~\citep{kipnis2024metabench},\footnote{Analysis code and DIF audit scripts are available at \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/dif-audit}.} we find that 31\% of MMLU~\citep{hendrycks2021mmlu} items receive ETS Category~C classification ($|\Delta_{\mathrm{MH}}| \geq 1.5$, $p < 0.05$) between 2023 and 2024 model cohorts---versus 0.18\% under a random-split control. This instability does not threaten benchmark validity ($\rho \approx 0.997$ between full and stable-item rankings); it is diagnostic, revealing which capability dimensions shift across model generations.

tool_args.old_string: \item \textbf{Temporal DIF audit framework}: We develop and validate an audit framework addressing three challenges specific to LLM benchmarks: (a)~cross-subject matching solves matching-variable contamination when the benchmark itself may be compromised ($\Delta\mathrm{FPR} = 0$ under single-subject contamination, $k \leq 5$; \Cref{sec:semisynthetic}); (b)~family-level DEFF correction handles non-independence among model families; (c)~semi-synthetic validation provides calibrated detection power absent ground-truth DIF labels. Replicated on GSM8K (\Cref{sec:gsm8k}).
tool_args.new_string: \item \textbf{Temporal DIF audit framework}: We develop and validate an audit framework addressing three challenges specific to LLM benchmarks: (a)~a novel cross-subject matching strategy solves matching-variable contamination when the benchmark itself may be compromised, with a constructive $\Delta\mathrm{FPR} = 0$ guarantee ($k \leq 5$; \Cref{sec:semisynthetic}); (b)~family-level DEFF correction, adapted from survey methodology, handles non-independence among model families; (c)~semi-synthetic validation provides calibrated detection power absent ground-truth DIF labels. Replicated on GSM8K (\Cref{sec:gsm8k}).
